chapter: Learning music and the early bands
title: Manuel Manetta, the Dutres and Eddie Atkins
summary: Stories of Manetta ('the horse') falling asleep on the streetcar after playing out at the lake, and of the Dutres and Eddie Atkins who played with George.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: He used to call him horse. Yeah, he called a horse.

Yeah. He used to call him horse. He used to call him horse. He used to call him horse. And I was talking about Manuel. I said I'd like to see Manuel. I hadn't seen him in a long time. And when they'd go play, they'd play out of the lake and come back, they'd grab him in the rainboard and George would be just coming home and sitting on Louisiana Avenue car and go to sleep. And they would bring him to the river, bring him back to Canal Street. And then when he'd come back and start the car stop, Franklin and Louisiana, they'd come up and wake him up and tell him, Go get off your corner, Mac. There's your corner. And wake him up. I said, Joe. He said, me and the horse had been walking from Farron Teller's, from Farron Teller up to the fair. And we'd get to the fair and we'd come back and walk again. I said, that's all you and Manuel can do. And when he'd get ready to come back, George, they would stand on the, wouldn't come in. They were scared because I'd call him out. I'd call him out. There wasn't but one of them. And I didn't know if you knew Manuel, Honorary Dutre. He was a slide with Eddie Atkins that played, now Eddie Atkins is another performer who played with my husband, slide drum. And Dutre. Honorary Dutre. I know Sam Dutre.
And his dad too. And Pete, you know Pete Dutre. Yeah. Well all of Dutres played with George.
